items.title: CVE-2026-76581 (CRITICAL 9.8): The WPMU DEV Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and…
items.one_liner: WPMU DEV Dashboard authentication bypass via HMAC flaws lets unauthenticated users gain administrator sessions.
items.summary: The WPMU DEV Dashboard plugin for WordPress up to version 5.0.1 suffers from an authentication bypass vulnerability due to inconsistent HMAC message construction between AJAX actions. Step 1 signs and discloses a concatenation including the domain, while Step 2 verifies a concatenation omitting the domain field. Unauthenticated attackers can obtain a valid HMAC from step 1 and replay it to step 2 to achieve an authenticated administrator session.
key_facts: Affected product: WPMU DEV Dashboard plugin for WordPress <= 5.0.1
items.bottom_line: Inconsistent HMAC verification in the WPMU DEV Dashboard plugin allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack administrator accounts.

items.one_liner: A critical zero-day in PTC supply chain software highlights the ongoing risk of mass extortion campaigns to enterprise infrastructure.
items.summary: The Clop cybercrime group exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM to conduct a massive data-theft extortion campaign against major global corporations. PTC disclosed the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-12569, on June 17, but attackers had already compromised victims as early as June using custom web shells designed for credential theft and lateral movement. Affected organizations include Toast and Zebra, while companies like GE, Philips, and Shell have not commented on the demands. Security researchers note that Clop routinely goes inactive between campaigns before deploying purpose-built toolkits to target sensitive supply-chain software.

items.title: CSS:the bomb inside your inbox
items.one_liner: Webmail CSS sanitizer bypasses and overlooked HTML label elements enable attackers to hijack user interfaces and manipulate Microsoft Outlook.
items.summary: PortSwigger researcher Gareth Heyes has published a security analysis detailing how discrepancies between webmail CSS sanitizers and browser rendering engines can be weaponized to hijack user interfaces, exfiltrate tokens, and steal credentials. The research highlights that HTML label elements are frequently overlooked by sanitizers and can inherit form click actions to manipulate application interfaces. Specifically, a vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook allows an attacker using a crafted email message to control the Outlook UI ribbon and pin messages without user interaction. The paper also examines how CSS pseudo-elements like :before and :after can inject hidden content to execute indirect prompt attacks against AI-driven browsers such as OpenAI Atlas.
key_facts: Affected products: Outlook, Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail, Fastmail, ProtonMail, Gmail, OpenAI Atlas
items.bottom_line: Discrepancies between HTML sanitizers and browser parsing engines allow attackers to execute privilege escalation and UI redressing via standard email messages.

items.title: Beyond the Payload: How User Invocation Shapes Coding Agent Vulnerability to Repository Poisoning
items.one_liner: User prompt choices significantly dictate the security of coding agents, with certain task types and prompt styles creating silent attack surfaces.
items.summary: Coding agent vulnerability to repository poisoning is heavily influenced by 'Prompt-Level Configurations' (PLCs) chosen by the user. A study using the CIPR benchmark across 20 repositories found that task type can create a 4.5-fold difference in attack success rates, with test-execution tasks being particularly dangerous due to high success and low alert rates. Furthermore, underspecified or noisy prompts can inadvertently suppress security alerts, making malicious content less conspicuous to the agent.
items.bottom_line: Coding agent security is not a static property but a dynamic outcome of user-side prompt configurations, where specific task types and prompt styles can bypass security alerts.

items.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems
items.one_liner: ECLIPSE uses self-evolving tool chains to execute stealthy, multi-step prompt injection attacks against long-horizon LLM agents.
items.summary: ECLIPSE is a self-evolving prompt injection framework designed to compromise long-horizon LLM agents through a combination of direct user instructions and indirect tool-side injections. It utilizes Stealthy Attack Trajectory Synthesis to verify candidate tool chains in a sandbox and Tool-Chain Steering via static workflow encoding and dynamic trajectory correction to keep agent execution on track. To evaluate the framework, researchers introduced LASE-Bench, featuring 120 malicious tasks and 198 unique tools. Experiments demonstrated that ECLIPSE achieved up to 96.7 percent attack success without defense and 69.2 percent under common safety filters.
key_facts: Benchmark: LASE-Bench with 120 malicious tasks and 198 unique tools
items.bottom_line: Long-horizon LLM agents are highly vulnerable to self-evolving prompt injections that span multiple tool-use execution stages.

items.title: Safe to Resume? Breaking Execution Continuity of Agent Execution via Rollback
items.one_liner: Checkpointing AI agents for recovery creates new security vulnerabilities that allow attackers to bypass safety controls or manipulate stateful transactions.
items.summary: Checkpoint and rollback (C/R) mechanisms in persistent AI agents introduce significant security risks because they often restore states that never coexisted in a valid execution history. Researchers identified five failure modes, including stale external dependencies and inconsistent internal states, which can be exploited to bypass malware verification, perform unauthorized actions, or trigger double payments. The study demonstrates these vulnerabilities across popular frameworks like Hermes, Cline, and LangGraph. The findings highlight a critical gap between the state restored by a checkpoint and the dependencies required for secure, continuous operation.
items.bottom_line: Restoring an agent from a checkpoint is not inherently secure and can lead to exploitable inconsistencies in state and external effects.

claims.text: We further demonstrate their security impact through three end-to-end attacks on Hermes, Cline, and LangGraph, enabling malware-verification bypass, unauthorized mail forwarding, and double payment.

items.title: ActReal: System-Level Mobile Agents Challenge Mobile Automation Detection
items.one_liner: Mobile automation detection is failing because agents can now spoof physical sensor data to match their synthetic touch inputs.
items.summary: ActReal is a new attack framework that enables system-level mobile agents to bypass automation detection by generating synchronized touch and IMU sensor data. By controlling both the touchscreen input and the application-visible sensor delivery, the agent creates realistic, time-aligned physical signals that mimic human interaction. The framework achieves a 77.5% success rate in event-level attacks, even when security systems monitor both touch and IMU signals simultaneously. This demonstrates that current mobile automation defenses are insufficient against adaptive, system-level agents.
items.bottom_line: Existing mobile security controls relying on touch and IMU correlation are effectively bypassed by this agent-based attack.

items.title: JITterFlip: Uncovering Fault Attack Surfaces in JIT-Compiled LLM Serving
items.one_liner: JIT compilers in LLM serving stacks are vulnerable to bit-flip attacks that can disrupt inference or cause massive latency spikes.
items.summary: JITterFlip is a new bit-flip attack (BFA) that targets the host-side JIT compiler control plane in GPU-based LLM serving environments. By faulting CPU-resident serving decisions, the attack can force gibberish outputs or trigger 'correct-output sponge' attacks that significantly amplify latency. The researchers demonstrated that these faults are transferable across models and can bypass existing BFA defenses. Furthermore, they showed that a single bit flip in CPU-resident branch code can propagate across the CPU-GPU boundary to disrupt GPU-executed inference.
items.bottom_line: Your LLM serving infrastructure's JIT compiler is a critical attack surface that can be exploited via Rowhammer to disrupt GPU inference.

claims.text: JITterFlip is the first BFA targeting the host-side JIT serving control plane of GPU-based LLM inference.

items.title: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
items.one_liner: A new self-improving red-teaming tool demonstrates that computer use agents are highly vulnerable to adaptive indirect prompt injection attacks that bypass safety checks.
items.summary: Researchers developed SIR, a self-improving red-teaming framework that uses an iterative feedback loop to generate stealthy indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks against computer use agents (CUAs). By diagnosing failed attack trajectories and distilling them into new strategies, SIR significantly increases attack success rates compared to hand-written baselines. The attacks target the operating system level, allowing adversaries to manipulate filesystems and services while maintaining the appearance of benign task completion. The discovered attack principles transfer across different model architectures without requiring additional feedback.
items.bottom_line: Computer use agents are vulnerable to adaptive, self-improving prompt injection attacks that can manipulate OS-level actions while remaining stealthy.

claims.text: Composing principles with feedback raises the attack success rate over a baseline written by hand, for example from 4% to 24% on Claude Opus 4.8 and from 0% to 28% on Gemini 3.5 Flash, while the benign task still completes.

items.title: Extracting Knowledge from Tools in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: LLM agents can inadvertently leak private database content through tool-mediated knowledge extraction attacks.
items.summary: ToolSiphon is a query-only extraction attack that recovers sensitive source data from LLM agents that use knowledge-based tools. The attack addresses tool-selection uncertainty and argument compression by using 'Tool Contrastive Analysis' to steer queries and 'Evidence Chained Feedback' to improve factual recovery. Experiments across three tool types and six datasets show the method can recover over 74% of source records, demonstrating a significant privacy risk for agents integrated with private databases.
items.bottom_line: Agents using knowledge-based tools are vulnerable to query-only extraction attacks that can reconstruct significant portions of the underlying data source.

items.title: Your secrets are leaking to AI coding agents (and how to stop it)
items.one_liner: AI coding agents automatically ingest and leak local configuration secrets into third-party prompt logs, creating persistent supply-chain risks.
items.summary: AI coding agents frequently leak sensitive data by automatically reading local project configuration files like environment variables and transmitting them as prompt context to external model providers. Because these prompts are stored in provider and gateway logs, secrets embedded in project files propagate to third-party systems without direct user interaction. Attackers are actively targeting this behavior through supply-chain threats like Mini Shai-Hulud, which searches agent context windows for cloud credentials, SSH keys, and wallet files. Remediating these exposures is difficult because leaked secrets remain in third-party logs long after local codebases are cleaned or keys are rotated.
key_facts:
Environment variables targeted: 80+
File paths targeted: 130+
Remediation median time: 94 days
items.bottom_line: Developers must proactively block local secrets from reaching AI agent contexts, as provider logs retain historical prompt data indefinitely.

items.title: Two Unitree G1 EDU Humanoid Robot Flaws Enable Root RCE, One Starts Over Bluetooth
items.one_liner: Two independent root RCE chains affect Unitree G1 EDU robots via network-adjacent and BLE vectors.
items.summary: Security researcher Olivier Laflamme has disclosed two root remote code execution flaws affecting the Unitree G1 EDU humanoid robot, tracked as CVE-2026-76639 and CVE-2026-76640. The first vulnerability involves a network-adjacent path traversal in chat_go that reaches bashrunner on the Locomotion PC. The second flaw initiates via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) proximity without pairing, exploiting an authorization gap in Unitree's cloud service where account-to-robot ownership checks were missing. This allowed key material recovery to establish authenticated BLE states and trigger a buffer overflow in Wi-Fi provisioning. Unitree patched the cloud ownership check in July 2026, but fixed firmware versions for the robot itself remain unconfirmed.

CVE-2026-76640: BLE proximity buffer overflow to root RCE
Target: Unitree G1 EDU Locomotion PC

items.title: Automated Researchers Can Reliably Mitigate Alignment Failures
items.one_liner: Automated alignment research methods can effectively discover training configurations that fix model safety failures better than human experts.
items.summary: Researchers investigate whether automated alignment researchers (AARs) can post-train models to mitigate common safety failures such as deception, sycophancy, and jailbreaks while preserving overall capabilities. Across 10 distinct alignment benchmarks, the top AAR methods successfully reduced targeted failures and generalized to held-out evaluations and larger models up to 4.7 times the size of the target. Interestingly, AAR methods outperformed human researchers given eight hours for the same task, and providing human research directions did not improve AAR performance. These findings indicate that automating alignment research on well-characterized vulnerabilities is becoming practical.

items.one_liner: useAgent turns LLM coding assistants into durable, sandboxed team coworkers with secure tool access and team context.
items.summary: useAgent is an open-source platform that transforms existing AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode into team coworkers equipped with isolated cloud Linux sandboxes, tools, and company context. items.one_liner: Tech Ai: single report, unconfirmed.
items.summary: Stop making AI agents watch the same video twice. CDAF is an open sidecar format for video: a plain-text, timestamped description that lives next to the video file with the same basename. Generate it once, and every AI agent that touches that footage afterward reads a few hundred text tokens instead of running a full video-understanding pass.
